extracted.intended_audience: experimental natural philosophers and optics researchers (scientists testing theories of light and colour)
extracted.subtask_short: experimental testing of light and color theories
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating experiments to test hypotheses about refraction and the nature of colours (Newton's programme). Includes specific experimental questions, controls (equal incidences), and guidance on which experiments are decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper method for inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: The proper method for inquiring after the properties of things, is to deduce them from experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theory should be derived from experiments that conclude positively and directly. One should enumerate all possible explanations and then use experiments to decide among them rather than relying on purely hypothetical reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test theories by whether proposed experiments prove their parts
rubrics_metrics.description: The way to examine it is by considering, whether the experiments which I proposed do prove those parts of the theory to which they are applied; or by prosecuting other experiments which the theory may suggest for its examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a theory by directly testing the specific claims it makes; design additional experiments suggested by the theory to probe its implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objections must be experimental or show experimental insufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: I could wish all objections were suspended, taken from hypothesis or any other heads than these two; of showing the insufficiency of experiments to determine these quaeries, or of producing other experiments which directly contradict me.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical responses should either (a) identify concrete defects in the experimental design/measurements, or (b) produce alternative experiments whose results directly contradict the theory. Avoid objections based solely on alternate hypotheses without experimental evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query 1: unequal refractions at equal incidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether rays, that are alike incident on the same medium, have unequal refractions; and how great are the inequalities of their refractions at any incidence?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design measurements comparing refraction of differently coloured rays under identical incidence angles to quantify any differences in refraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query 2: law governing degree of refraction
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the law according to which each ray is more or less refracted; whether it be that the same ray is ever refracted according to the same ratio of the sines of incidence and refraction; and divers rays, according to divers ratios; or that the refraction of each ray is greater or less without any certain rule?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether refraction follows a consistent mathematical law (e.g. same sine-ratio per ray) or varies irregularly across rays. Requires systematic measurements across incidences and ray types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query 3: constant colours for particular refrangibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether rays which are endued with particular degrees of refrangibility, when they are by any means separated, have particular colours constantly belonging to them, viz. the least refrangible, scarlet; the most refrangible, deep violet; the middle, sea-green; and others, other colours?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test whether particular refrangibility aligns consistently with particular colours by separating rays and observing colour assignments repeatedly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query 4: does refraction change ray colour
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the colour of any sort of rays apart may be changed by refraction?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate whether passage through media (refraction) can alter the intrinsic colour of a ray, not merely separate mixed rays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query 5: coalescing rays and colour change vs mixing
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether colours by coalescing do really change one another to produce a new colour, or produce it by mixing only?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between genuine transformational interactions of rays (coalescence yielding new colours) and simple additive/superpositional mixing effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query 6: mixture of rays reproducing sunlight
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a due mixture of rays, indued with all variety of colours, produces light perfectly like that of the sun, and which has all the same properties, and exhibits the same phaenomena?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt to recombine separated component rays to see whether their mixture reproduces the complete properties and phenomena of ordinary sunlight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query 7: are component colours really changed or merely separated
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the component colours of each mixture be really changed; or be only separated, when from that mixture various colours are produced again by refraction?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When mixtures yield colours under refraction, determine whether component colours have been altered (chemical/physical change) or simply spatially separated and recombined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query 8: are there other colours from refraction than from separated rays
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there be any other colours, produced by refraction, than such as ought to result from the colours belonging to the diversely refrangible rays, by their being separated or mixed by that refraction?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search for colours arising from refraction that are not accounted for by separation/mixing of the hypothesised differently refrangible rays; i.e., look for anomalous phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control: measure refractions from equal incidences
rubrics_metrics.description: If he has any doubt of our experiment, I request that he may measure the refractions of the said rays of divers colours from equal incidences, and he will then see that they are unequal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure incidence angles are equal when comparing refractive behaviour of different rays; use small immoveable holes or other apparatus to guarantee equal incidence. This is a key control to rule out unequal incidence as a confound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish laws of refraction before addressing nature of colours
rubrics_metrics.description: The laws of refraction being thoroughly inquired into and determined before the nature of colours be taken into consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat foundational optical laws (quantitative refraction behaviour) as prerequisites; do not build claims about colour origin until those laws are settled experimentally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and conditions for liquid colour-mixing experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: This experiment requires liquors of full and intense colours, which transmit very few rays besides those of their own colours; such as rarely occur, as will be seen by illuminating liquors with different prismatic colours in a dark room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use strongly coloured, highly selective liquids (transmitting mostly their own colour). Prefer experiments with liquids in separate vessels rather than premixed, because mixing may induce chemical interactions (change of texture, opacity) that confound optical interpretation. Prefer opposite colour pairings (red/blue, yellow/violet, green/purple) for clearer effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware chemical/physical interactions in mixing media
rubrics_metrics.description: Many liquors act mutually on each other, and acquire a new texture of parts; hence they may become opaque, or diaphanous, or of various colours, in no manner owing to the colours of the compound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not infer optical principles from colour changes in mixed media without ruling out chemical/physical changes; such experiments are less proper for proving optical doctrine and are better used to illustrate or suggest hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of calculation errors: neglect negligible niceties
rubrics_metrics.description: The breadth of the hole in the posterior surface, if such there be, would hardly produce an error of two seconds; and in practice such niceties may well be neglected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate the magnitude of possible sources of error; if they are below the practical resolution of the measurement, they can be justifiably neglected. Still, note them and consider whether more precise methods are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer direct, demonstrative, repeatable experimental procedures (anatomical example)
rubrics_metrics.description: A more easy experiment to be made, which is more demonstrative; viz. open a dog at a convenient distance of time from his feeding, and then tie a ligature on the ductus thoracicus nigh the subclavian; your receptaculum chyli will continue full, 48 hours or longer if you please...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When testing anatomical/physiological claims, use direct and repeatable manipulations (e.g., ligature to observe natural distension) rather than complex injections that may fail because of valves or produce misleading effects. Validate by multiple complementary techniques (injection with a coagulating composition to trace channels vs ligature/distension observation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design experiments to avoid ambiguous interventions (injections vs natural flow)
rubrics_metrics.description: The way of syringing a liquor which is apt to coagulation into the ductus thoracicus... I think to be needless and unprofitable as to this inquiry, when there is a more easy experiment to be made, which is more demonstrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious with interventions that can alter or obstruct natural pathways (coagulating injections, heating). Prefer minimal interventions that reveal natural behaviour; account for anatomical valves and structures that can prevent passage of injected substances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use symmetry/equality in prism geometry to infer refrangibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Since I supposed the refractions at the side AC are nearly equal to those at the side BC; if AC and BC be equal, the inclination of the rays GH and Lm, to the base AB of the prism, will be similar; and therefore... the refracted rays HI and mn will be also equal, provided the rays FL and KG be equally refrangible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit geometric symmetry (equal prism faces, equal incidence positions) to isolate variables; if geometry and incidence are controlled, any observed difference in emerging angles implicates differences in refrangibility of the rays rather than geometric artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility and use of multiple methods
rubrics_metrics.description: If he dislikes the manner in which I have performed this matter... it is easy to devise other ways; as indeed I myself have tried several other methods with advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm key experimental findings with alternative methods to rule out artefacts of a single setup. Repeatability across distinct procedures strengthens conclusions.
